items.title: Signal replies keep reaching a session across its own turns
items.why: Owner 2026-10-29: replying from Signal while a session waits does not reach it. Seen in this session: every self-started turn (a background agent's report) fires UserPromptSubmit, so quiet() stops the listener and turns away off; listeners/ was empty while the owner thought a reply would land. The next listener only knows its own message, so a reply quoting the earlier one is dropped.
items.promise: quiet() treats a self-started turn (a prompt carrying the task-notification wrapper or the wake text) like a Signal wake: the listener and the away switch stay as they are. A reply quoting or tagging any message a session sent while its turns continue reaches that session's current listener, not only the latest message. Typed prompts at the Mac still stop the listener and turn away off.
acceptance: Given a session waiting on Signal, when a UserPromptSubmit carrying a task-notification arrives, then the listener keeps running and away stays on.
Given a session whose listener was replaced by a later turn's listener, when the owner quotes the earlier message, then the reply wakes that session.
Given a prompt typed at the Mac, when quiet() runs, then the listener stops and away turns off, as today.

acceptance: Given a UserPromptSubmit opening with an agent-message or ci-monitor-event wrapper, when quiet() runs, then the listener keeps running and away stays on.

items.title: Probe asyncRewake: headless runs and more than 8 Signal wakes
items.why: Riskiest unknown first: the binary suggests claude -p runs this Stop hook synchronously (up to 300 s at the Mac, 3600 s away) and that wakes may cap at 8; one hour of probing decides install-guards.
items.promise: A run, not a change. In a new scratch folder (not this repo, whose untracked .claude/settings.local.json carries the owner's live relay hooks), with throwaway hooks, measure on Claude Code 2.1.311 and record with wuwei plan run: (1) whether claude -p waits for a Stop hook marked asyncRewake; (2) how many consecutive asyncRewake wakes (exit 2) an interactive session takes with no typed prompt, past 8; (3) what the woken turns' Stop input and the hook environment carry (stop_hook_active, and the variable that marks a print-mode run, such as CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT), so install-guards can tell a headless run apart. Outside: any change to signal_cc. If wakes stop at 8 or fewer, file the follow-up before closing.
acceptance: Given a scratch folder whose .claude/settings.local.json holds a Stop hook with asyncRewake true that sleeps 20 s and then writes a marker file, when claude -p 'reply ok' runs there, then the record states the wall time and whether the run waited for the hook.

Given an interactive claude session in a detached screen with an asyncRewake Stop hook that exits 2 with 'reply with the next number' up to 12 times and logs each call, when one typed prompt starts it and nobody types again, then the record states how many wakes happened and whether the 9th to 12th did.

Given both hooks log their stdin and the names of their environment variables, when they run in print mode and in interactive mode, then the record lists stop_hook_active for each call and the variable that tells the two modes apart, with no secret values copied.
Given wakes stop at or before the 9th, when the run is recorded, then a follow-up item names the cap and a mitigation (for example a Signal notice that the session needs a prompt typed at the Mac).
items.domain: complex: what Claude Code 2.1.311 does shows only by running it; its binary reads CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP ?? 8 and backgrounds asyncRewake only when the session is interactive or has streaming input, which suggests but does not prove both risks
items.reason: Claude Code 2.1.311: claude -p waits for an asyncRewake Stop hook (38-40 s run, 21 s hook); an interactive session took 12 consecutive wakes with no typed prompt (calls 9-12 ran, no cap hit); stop_hook_active false on the first Stop, true on woken turns; CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT is sdk-cli in print mode and cli interactively, but a child inherits claude-desktop from the desktop app, so install-guards must not trust an inherited value. No follow-up needed.

Given a prompt that times out, a stream that ends, or the owner returning to the Mac, when ask returns, then that line's outcome names which.

items.title: Relay plan approval (ExitPlanMode) to Signal
items.why: G-2 follow-up and a trust-boundary change, so it carries spec artifacts and a probe-first step; lands after land-status-ci.
items.promise: Plan approval (ExitPlanMode) reaches Signal while the owner is away. The relay sends the plan (cut past a limit, with its full length noted) and a poll: approve and keep asking for each edit; approve and auto-accept edits; keep planning. A thumbs-up approves with edits still asked; a thumbs-down or n keeps planning; any other reply keeps planning with the reply as feedback. Approval without a choice keeps per-edit prompts. README's Security section says what is now relayed. First step, before building: a throwaway PermissionRequest hook in a scratch folder records what Claude Code does after allow, with and without a mode change, and the spec cites it. Files: signal_cc/domain/forms.py, signal_cc/domain/texts.py, signal_cc/entry/hooks.py, tests/test_domain.py, tests/test_app.py, tests/test_adapters.py, README.md, and the spec engine's artifacts. Outside: anything while the owner is at the Mac; bypass-permissions mode.
acceptance: Given a session in plan mode calls ExitPlanMode while the owner is away, when the PermissionRequest hook runs, then Signal gets the plan with its tag and a poll of the three choices.
Given the owner votes the first choice or reacts thumbs-up, when the hook returns, then the session leaves plan mode and later edits still ask for permission.
Given the owner votes auto-accept, when the hook returns, then the session's mode is the accept-edits mode the probe recorded.
Given the owner replies 'add a migration step' quoting the plan, when the hook returns, then the decision denies with that text as feedback and the session keeps planning.
Given a plan longer than the limit, when it is sent, then the text is cut with the total length noted and the poll still arrives.
Given the owner is at the Mac, when ExitPlanMode is called, then nothing is sent to Signal.
items.domain: complex: it lifts a refusal the README promises (Security: plan approval stays on the Mac), and which permission mode Claude Code takes after a hook allows ExitPlanMode shows only once built
